rows.subtype: Approach: delays because the task feels too big [Thinking]
rows.description: A teenager with a long essay keeps scrolling on his phone. The size of the task makes him feel small, so he avoids even opening the file.
A teenager delays a project because a poor result would reveal weakness; putting it off protects the self-image but makes the eventual work worse.
The person commits to five minutes, sets up the workspace the night before and forgives past delays. Starting small breaks the dread, and kindness to oneself makes it easier to face the next task.

rows.subtype: Restless and asking what to do [Actor]
rows.description: A child declares boredom after ten minutes and wants a screen; boredom is uncomfortable but can also be the doorway to imagination when adults give time and simple materials.
After a weekend binge, a student checks what triggered it, an argument and boredom, adjusts by planning an outing for the next weekend, and restarts the next day instead of quitting.
A child who stumbles while reading makes a silly face and gets the class laughing with them; the joke keeps control of the moment, though constant clowning can hide worry.

Colleagues call me "too sincere" and "not practical" for refusing shortcuts. It hurts to be mocked for integrity. Wise: hold my line with humour and skill, and find allies. Harmful: turning self-righteous.
